summary.headline: Thomas Cook India Q2 FY27 consolidated PBT before exceptionals held at INR 848 million (flat YoY) as income fell 5% to INR 20,030 million.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income fell 5% YoY to INR 20,030 million, but PBT before exceptional items was flat at INR 848 million and PBT margin rose to 4.2% from 4.0%. Financial Services was the standout, with revenue up 21% and EBIT margin at 44.1%. The India travel business recovered through the quarter, with the India EBIT deficit narrowing from 31% to 22%, while West Asia-exposed businesses (Desert Adventures, DEI, AlliedTPro) remained well below last year but improved sequentially. Sterling Holiday Resorts delivered its highest-ever Q2 revenue of about INR 1,272 million (+17%), with reported EBITDA diluted by a one-off-like GST input tax credit cost of about INR 40 million.

segments.name: Financial Services (Thomas Cook forex)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue +21% with gross turnover INR 39 billion (+7%); EBIT INR 452 million, margin 44.1%. Retail turnover +12%, education forex +33% against a 34% fall in industry education remittances; corporate +10%, travel -6%.

segments.name: India Travel (B2C, domestic, DMS, corporate)
segments.commentary: India EBIT deficit narrowed from 31% to 22%; domestic B2C grew 8%, India DMS grew 16%, corporate travel revenue +11% to INR 446 million. B2C overall fell 17% on long-haul outbound weakness, with Kailash Mansarovar cancellations of INR 185 million.

segments.name: International DMS (Desert Adventures, AlliedTPro, Asian Trails)
segments.commentary: Desert Adventures sales down 67% (vs 89% in Q1); AlliedTPro down 22% (vs 40% gap in Q1); overall overseas DMS revenue -7%, Asian Trails +9%, South Africa private safaris +31%.

segments.name: Sterling Holiday Resorts
segments.commentary: Q2 room nights +23%, occupancy +300 bps, average rate +12%, RevPAR +12%; 7 resorts opened to 83 properties and over 4,000 keys. Q2 EBITDA hit by about INR 40 million GST input tax credit cost not present last year.

segments.name: DEI (Digiphoto)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 147 crore vs INR 130 crore in Q1 and INR 195 crore LY (about -22% YoY); EBIT loss of about INR 1.2 crore vs loss of INR 15 crore in Q1 and profit of INR 2.3 crore LY. UAE revenue back to 40-50% of prior year.

guidance_outlook: India leisure forward bookings for OND quarter up about 30% YoY in value terms; long-haul booking window D-60 to D-120, short-haul about D-30, domestic D-7 to D-15.
Desert Adventures expects about 50% recovery in the current quarter.
DEI expects a steady Middle East recovery and a much better Q3, its largest quarter, assuming no further disruption.
Sterling expects stronger revenue and earnings conversion in H2 as new resorts mature and GST cost comparability normalises from Q3.
Financial Services expected to sustain double-digit growth with EBIT margin in the 40-45% range.
Sterling long-term healthy EBITDA margin range of 32% to 37%, depending on seasonality.
Sterling demerger: NCLT shareholder meeting directive expected within days, meeting around end-December or early January, NCLT approval targeted by end-March or early April.
capex_capacity: Sterling opened 7 resorts in Q2 (6 management contracts, 1 revenue share), taking portfolio to 83 properties and over 4,000 keys; 3 of these are wildlife properties opened in September.
Sterling ramp-up: first 90 days treated as a 'baby phase'; full ramp takes 2-3 seasons, faster for wildlife properties opened ahead of peak season.
Sterling remains asset-light and capital-light, with growth planned via management contracts and revenue share.
Financial Services: retail counters operationalised at Angamaly, Cochin and Hubli; Thiruvananthapuram branches closed.
Thomas Cook franchise branch network at 310 (vs 289 a year ago), a record high.
DEI closed around 30-32 non-profitable sites in the quarter; approximately 230 sites remain, with 8-10% estimated to be EBITDA-negative and all sites kept gross-margin positive.
Post-visit sales activated across 45% of DEI sites by count and 35% by revenue.
demand_pricing: Financial Services: LRS data shows education outbound remittances down 34% and travel remittances down 1% (Apr-Aug 2026); Thomas Cook education forex grew 33%. Gross forex margin about 1.6-1.8%; float yield about 7.5-8%.

Sterling: average rate up about 12% to near INR 6,500 in Q2; H1 ARR +11%; H1 occupancy +500 bps and room nights +24%. Membership acquisition stopped since 2023; about 65,000-70,000 members, about 35,000 travel each year.
Sterling GST: input tax credit no longer available on room rates of INR 7,500 and below, which created about INR 40 million of Q2 cost.
Travel: China visa rejections and high airfares hurt long-haul outbound; Europe and Australia long-haul rebounding; Japan trending well.
Corporate travel: air transaction volume +18%, hotel volumes +81%, online booking tool adoption 32%.
Overall digital adoption in forex rose to 22.4% from 21.5%; forex cards sold via Blinkit grew 96% vs Q3 FY26 (not like-for-like).

qa_highlights.question: How long does a new Sterling resort take to reach mature profitability, and is the 30% forward booking figure in value or passenger terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikram Lalvani: first 90 days are a baby phase, with the real ramp after; full maturity in 2-3 seasons, faster if opened before peak season (wildlife opened in September may ramp in about 2.5 months). Mahesh Iyer: the 30% forward booking growth is in value terms, OND 2025 vs OND 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Sterling EBIT growth lower than revenue growth, and what is the long-term margin and KPI framework?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikram Lalvani: about INR 40 million of GST input tax credit cost in Q2 with no prior-year equivalent (ITC restriction on sub-INR 7,500 rates began late September 2025); ex-GST EBITDA would be about INR 329 million, up 19-20%. Healthy EBITDA margin range 32-37%; no precise FY28 number given, growth to continue at the trend of the past 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 21% Financial Services revenue growth, any one-offs, and what sustainable growth and margin to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahesh Iyer: retail grew about 12%, led by education (+33%) via NBFC tie-ups, new counsellor relationships and share gains; corporate +10%; no one-offs cited. Expect double-digit growth going forward, with EBIT margin of 40-45%.

qa_highlights.question: How will Thomas Cook deploy about INR 28 billion of cash and short-term investments, and are acquisitions planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Debasis Nandy: a large part is prepaid forex card float, net debt position about INR 316 crore gross basis, so free cash is much lower. Uses: automation/AI, SAP modernisation, liquidity buffer, and acquisitions only if in-line and price-accretive; otherwise cash returns, with Sterling demerger (holding about INR 380 crore cash) cited as a reward.

qa_highlights.question: Does replacing legacy members with free independent guests lift RevPAR per occupied room and what is the demerger timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikram Lalvani: members are still serviced, not displaced; guest ratio is the metric and members are about 10-12% of room nights and rising supply disperses them. Debasis Nandy: SEBI, BSE and NSE approvals received, NCLT hearing held, shareholder meeting expected end-December or early January, NCLT approval targeted by end-March or early April.

qa_highlights.question: What is Financial Services' gross spread, float yield and why did margins improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahesh Iyer: blended gross margin about 1.6-1.8%, float yield about 7.5-8%. Margin improvement attributed to retail growth (student and corporate), digital shift with low incremental cost, and efficiencies; referenced slide 8 for trends (gross turnover CAGR 22% FY22-FY26).

risks_watch: International DMS recovery is still fragile: Desert Adventures sales down 67% and AlliedTPro down 22% in Q2, with management guiding only to a 50% recovery at Desert Adventures in the current quarter and conditioning all outlooks on no new geopolitical disruption.

Sterling GST input tax credit restriction on room rates of INR 7,500 and below cost about INR 40 million in Q2 and will keep affecting reported EBITDA comparisons until Q3 laps it; reported Sterling EBITDA growth was only about 4-5% against 19-20% ex-GST.

Forward bookings: the 30% OND growth is in value terms and is concentrated in India outbound; long-haul China visa rejections and elevated airfares remain a drag, and the Q3 forward-booking numbers are not yet visible in revenue.

Sterling demerger timeline: NCLT shareholder-meeting directive expected within days, meeting around end-December or early January, NCLT approval targeted by end-March or early April; any slippage affects the FY28 listing plan.

Financial Services growth depends on the education segment, which grew 33% against a 34% fall in industry education remittances; management did not say how sustainable share gains are if the student segment softens further. Watch the gross margin of about 1.6-1.8% and float yield of about 7.5-8% as rates move.
key_quotes: Our Q2 performance has helped us recover a good part of the ground we lost earlier in the year because of geopolitical volatility, and we have been able to narrow that gap quite efficiently, as I just mentioned.

Excluding this incremental GST cost for analytical comparison, EBITDA would have actually been approximately INR 329 million, representing a growth of around 19% to 20% over the corresponding quarter last year compared to a reported growth of approximately 4% to 5%.
Our forward booking numbers that we have quoted is a 30% value growth compared to the same quarter last year, which is OND '25 compared to OND '26.
We are expecting them to issue us that directive in the next few days to hold the shareholders' meeting, and we'll get 60 days to hold that.
summary.management_tone: Confident on India travel, Financial Services and Sterling, where management cited specific numbers and a stronger second half. Cautious on international businesses (Desert Adventures, AlliedTPro, DEI, long-haul outbound), with repeated caveats that outlooks depend on no further geopolitical disruption, and vague on Sterling's long-term KPIs (no FY28 figure given).

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Sterling is capital-light via management contracts and revenue share, Sterling holds about INR 3,805 million net cash, and the company is focused on automation and SAP modernisation rather than new physical capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided double-digit Financial Services growth at 40-45% EBIT margin and a much better DEI Q3, but the travel and international recovery is conditional on no further geopolitical disruption.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Desert Adventures sales were down 67% and AlliedTPro down 22% in Q2, with only a 50% Desert Adventures recovery guided, and all outlooks are conditioned on no new geopolitical disruption; long-haul China visa rejections and high airfares are a drag.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Not discussed beyond Sterling resort additions, which are already counted under capacity.

rows.label: Sterling demerger and listing
rows.why: NCLT shareholder meeting around end-December or early January with approval targeted by end-March or early April; SEBI, BSE and NSE approvals already received, though slippage would affect the FY28 listing plan.

rows.label: DEI Middle East recovery and Q3 seasonality
rows.why: DEI Q2 revenue was INR 147 crore (-22% YoY) with EBIT loss of about INR 1.2 crore vs INR 15 crore loss in Q1, and management expects a much better Q3, its largest quarter, assuming no further disruption; about 230 sites remain after closing 30-32 non-profitable ones.

rows.label: Sterling GST ITC cost laps from Q3
rows.why: About INR 40 million of Q2 cost from ITC restriction on room rates of INR 7,500 and below has no prior-year equivalent, so reported Sterling EBITDA growth of 4-5% should normalise toward the 19-20% ex-GST rate after Q3.
